title: Colonization of Aposymbiotic Aiptasia with Symbiodinium
author: Grossman Lab
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rh4d38w

steps.title: Pre‑condition anemones one month
steps.instruction: Place anemones in a clear container for one month before infection and expose them to 12 h light per day at 20–40 µmol photons · m⁻² · s⁻¹.

steps.title: Screen for existing algae
steps.instruction: A few days before infection, examine all anemones under a fluorescence stereomicroscope using a suitable filter set and ~20× total magnification to detect any chlorophyll fluorescence.

steps.title: Determine Symbiodinium cell density
steps.instruction: Count intact, pigmented Symbiodinium cells in the culture with a hemocytometer or flow cytometer; aim for a density between 100 000 and 1 000 000 cells · ml⁻¹.

steps.title: Prepare inoculum volume
steps.instruction: Calculate the culture volume needed to reach a final concentration of at least 10 000 cells · ml⁻¹ in the anemone tank (use exactly 10 000 cells · ml⁻¹ for infection experiments) and collect that volume.

steps.title: Pellet algae first spin
steps.instruction: Transfer the calculated culture volume into a centrifuge tube, spin 10 min at 5 000 × g, and resuspend the pellet in 1 ml artificial seawater.

steps.title: Wash algae second spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the suspension again for 10 min at 5 000 × g and resuspend the pellet in a fresh 1 ml of artificial seawater.

steps.title: Add algae and incubate overnight
steps.instruction: Add the algae suspension to the anemone tank, then incubate overnight at 27 °C with a 12 h light : 12 h dark cycle.

steps.title: Feed brine shrimp
steps.instruction: The next day, feed freshly hatched brine shrimp (or a homogenate of frozen brine shrimp) to the anemones to strongly enhance Symbiodinium uptake; feeding can be done in parallel with algae addition if desired.

steps.title: Clean tank after uptake
steps.instruction: After 2–6 h, clean the tank, perform a water change, and return the tank to the incubator (27 °C, 12 h light : 12 h dark).

steps.title: Maintain or sample colonization
steps.instruction: For experimental colonization, take samples every few days for up to 30 days without feeding, changing water regularly. If not an experiment, feed anemones 1–2 times per week with brine shrimp and change water after feeding.

steps.title: Monitor algae proliferation
steps.instruction: Observe the anemones under a fluorescence stereomicroscope; algae should become visible 2–10 days after infection, with whole‑animal coloration changes appearing later.
